items.title: Ideal Gas Equation in Terms of Boltzmann Constant

blocks.text: Here n represents number of moles of the ideal gas. It can be defined as the number of atoms are molecules per unit Avogadro's number (Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³).

blocks.title: Example 6.1
blocks.problem: One mole of an ideal gas is at a temperature of 300 K. If the Boltzmann constant is 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, calculate the volume of the gas at a pressure of 1 atom. [1atm = 101325 Pa]
steps: R = Nₐ × k_B   where   k_B = R/Nₐ
Here V = n × Nₐ × k_B × T / P
blocks.answer: Thus, volume of gas would be 0.03 m³.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The pressure is 1 atm (the book prints “1 atom”). The working gives 6.02 × 10²³ × 1.38 × 10⁻²³ × 300 / 101325 = 0.0246 m³, so the volume is about 0.025 m³ (24.6 litres), not 0.03 m³.
